clippingConclusion.meaning: A conservative sphere bound proves all source vertices and triangle interiors remain between .1 and100 for any orbit orientation under current center, camera distance/zoom .75..1.35 and hand transforms. This is stronger than sampling a finite set of yaw angles. It is not an app runtime test.
clippingConclusion.numericalCaveat: Python double arithmetic on authored JSON numbers; not bitwise RealityKit Float computation. Margins are several world units, far exceeding Float rounding.

canonicalPerspectiveFit.formula: At existing canonical transform, t=1.08*max(abs(y)/depth,abs(x)/(aspect*depth)), verticalFOV=2atan(t). All source vertices then have max absolute normalized x/y <=1/1.08=.9259259.
canonicalPerspectiveFit.limit: Each labeled aspect is an arithmetic example. The formula covers any finite positive aspect if representable FOV remains strictly between0 and180; exhaustive app layout coverage is not claimed.

preserved: Same target/canonical center, canonical offset, yaw direction, elevation clamp±.55, wrapping/full azimuth, zoom clamp .75..1.35 and reset conditions.

changed: Perspective introduces depth-dependent apparent size, foreshortening and parallax. It cannot reproduce orthographic pixels.

At canonical depth plane zoom gain is exactly the existing zoom factor. Other depths differ: conservative maxzoom1.35 relative gains span.9465…1.0910(single) and.9327…1.1401(pair) relative to orthographic zoom, across sphere bounds. These are bounds, not measured subjective effects.

Canonical8% framing margin does not promise full outline visible after orbit/zoom. At1.35, even flat central-plane geometry may exceed the .9259 canonical normalized extent. Existing orthographic zoom also allows edge cropping. Do not silently clamp/auto-refit or change gesture semantics to conceal this.
